messages.content: Oregon got tightened again. For Oct 13-17, Beaverton reception ends about 8:40 Monday, Salem first visit moved to 7:45 Tuesday, and the Albany transfer table Wednesday may run until 5:30. Salem breakfast rooms are thin, Albany/Corvallis rates are ridiculous, and my holds expire tonight. Can you rank the hotel options and the safest overnight sequence?

One choice affects reliability: after the Beaverton reception, are you willing to drive to Salem Monday night, or should I preserve a Beaverton night and build a very early Tuesday drive? The late drive is less pleasant, but it protects the 7:45 visit.
Drive Monday night if that is the safer call. I just need a food plan because arriving in Salem after 10 with no dinner would be ugly.

Then I would sequence it this way: Sun 10/13 Beaverton/Tanasbourne for the PDX arrival and Monday visits; Mon-Tue 10/14-15 Salem so Tuesday's 7:45 start is protected and Wednesday Albany is still easy; Wed 10/16 Eugene West/airport side after Albany. I would not overnight in Albany or Corvallis unless Wednesday starts before about 8:30, because the price spike does not buy much reliability.
Wednesday first thing is 9:15 in Albany. The table may end at 5:30. Does Tuesday Salem still hold up?

Yes. Leave Salem around 8:05 for the 9:15 Albany item and you still have a small cushion. After a 5:30 table, leave Albany by 5:45, reach the Eugene/West 11th area around 6:45-7:00, and still have normal dinner options before the Thursday morning program.

The holds are Cedar Hills/Tanasbourne in Beaverton, Hampton or Best Western in Salem, Comfort Suites Albany, Courtyard Corvallis, and Eugene West 11th or Springfield Gateway. How would you rank those?

My rank: 1) Beaverton Cedar Hills/Tanasbourne for Sunday only, whichever has easier parking and breakfast hours. 2) Hampton Salem for Mon-Tue if breakfast begins by 6:00 or 6:30 and parking is free. 3) Eugene West 11th/airport side for Wednesday because it keeps the flight day simpler. 4) Springfield Gateway as a backup if the Thursday venue shifts east. 5) Comfort Suites Albany only as a backup for an earlier Wednesday start. 6) Courtyard Corvallis last: high rate and not enough schedule benefit.
Can you put the confirm list under each hold? I need breakfast times, parking, cancellation cutoff, and late-arrival food.

Confirm these before releasing holds: Beaverton Sun: Monday breakfast start, parking cost or validation, 10/13 cancel cutoff, usually Sat 10/12 6 p.m. if it is 24-hour, and Sunday late food nearby. Salem Mon-Tue: Tuesday/Wednesday breakfast start, free parking, whether Sun 10/13 6 p.m. covers both nights or if it is per-night, and any 9:45-10:15 p.m. food. Albany/Corvallis backups: free-cancel date only; release if Salem works. Eugene West/Springfield: Thursday breakfast, free parking, 10/16 cancel cutoff, likely Tue 10/15 6 p.m., and restaurants open until at least 9.
If Hampton Salem breakfast starts by 6:30, keep that. If not, is Best Western acceptable?

Yes. Keep Hampton Salem first if breakfast starts by 6:30; otherwise use Best Western if it confirms earlier food and an itemized folio. Final keep list: Beaverton Sunday only, Salem Monday and Tuesday, Eugene West Wednesday, with Springfield as the Thursday-location backup. Cancel Albany and Corvallis once Salem and Eugene are confirmed. For Monday night, eat in Beaverton before driving or pick up something near Cedar Hills; do not count on Salem restaurants after 10.

messages.content: Oregon fares shifted, and I need to decide tonight. Monday midday SLC-PDX nonstop is cheaper and technically works for Beaverton if traffic cooperates. Sunday evening costs a bit more but is calmer. Coming home, EUG with a connection saves the Portland drive, while PDX nonstop is cheaper. The Beaverton, Salem, and Eugene holds all expire this evening. What would you book?

Can I optimize for protecting the Beaverton/Salem timing and avoiding the Portland backtrack if it stays within reimbursement? What airfare cap and one-way car fee tolerance did the coordinator give you?
Airfare under about $650 is fine, and the $72 one-way Avis fee is reimbursable if I explain it. Delta or Alaska is fine if close, economy, no two-stop itineraries. Window seats if the map allows.

Given that, I would book the safer pair. Sunday outbound: Delta nonstop SLC 5:55 p.m. to PDX 7:08 p.m., about $236, and it removes Monday arrival and traffic risk. Monday alternative: Delta nonstop SLC 12:15 p.m. to PDX 1:28 p.m., about $182, but it depends on an on-time arrival before the Beaverton reception. Return: Delta EUG 1:15 p.m. to SEA to SLC 6:31 p.m., about $304, with a 70-minute Seattle connection. The PDX nonstop is cheaper, but it adds the Eugene-to-Portland drive. Total airfare is around $540, inside the cap.
Is the Seattle connection comfortable enough? I do not want a sprint after the Eugene morning event.

Seventy minutes in Seattle on one ticket is workable with a carry-on; it is not generous, but it is not a red flag. There is a later Eugene option with about a 95-minute Seattle connection and a later SLC arrival for roughly $70 more. If getting home at a reasonable hour matters more, take the 1:15. If connection comfort matters more, take the later one.
Take the 1:15 if the booking page still shows at least an hour in Seattle. I would rather not get home after 9 if I can avoid it.

Then book Delta SLC-PDX Sunday evening and Delta EUG-SEA-SLC Thursday at 1:15 only if the Seattle connection is 60+ minutes. Select economy window seats where available. Avis: pick up at PDX Sunday around 7:45 p.m.; return at EUG by about 11:10 Thursday. Note the $72 one-way drop fee for reimbursement.
Which hotel holds do I actually book? I still have Beaverton, Hampton Salem, Best Western Salem, Albany, Corvallis, Eugene West, and Springfield.

Book these: TownePlace or the better Beaverton/Tanasbourne hold for Sunday only; Hampton Salem for Monday-Tuesday; Hampton Eugene West/airport side for Wednesday. Keep Best Western Salem as backup until Hampton confirms breakfast by 6:30 and itemized folio. Keep Springfield only if it remains no-penalty until the Thursday venue is firm; otherwise release it. Cancel Albany, Corvallis, and any extra Beaverton Monday. Meal note: eat in Beaverton before the Salem drive Monday; Eugene West 11th should have quick dinner options after Albany.
Can you write the reimbursement note and the cancellation reminders for my confirmation email?

Reimbursement note: Sunday PDX arrival selected to protect the Monday evening Beaverton event and Tuesday 7:45 Salem visit; Thursday EUG return selected to avoid a post-program drive back to PDX; Avis one-way fee is lower-risk than extra mileage and staff time. Reminders: Beaverton 10/13 cancel by Sat 10/12 6 p.m. if 24-hour; Salem 10/14-15 confirm whether Sun 10/13 6 p.m. covers both nights or if it is per-night; Eugene 10/16 cancel by Tue 10/15 6 p.m.; backup hotels release as soon as primary confirmations arrive.
Great. Give me the final booking summary, then I will buy the flights and rooms.

Final booking: Delta Sun 10/13 SLC 5:55 p.m. to PDX 7:08 p.m.; Delta Thu 10/17 EUG 1:15 p.m. via SEA to SLC about 6:31 p.m., only if the SEA connection is 60+ minutes. Economy, window seats where available. Avis PDX pickup around 7:45 p.m. Sunday, EUG return by 11:10 Thursday; save the $72 drop-fee note. Hotels: Beaverton/Tanasbourne Sunday, Hampton Salem Monday-Tuesday, Hampton Eugene West Wednesday. Keep Salem/Springfield backups only until breakfast and venue checks clear. Cancel Albany, Corvallis, PDX-return backup, and extra Beaverton night after confirmations. Verify breakfast hours, parking, and itemized folios on each confirmation.

messages.content: Quick Oregon repair: Thursday counselor breakfast moved from downtown Eugene to Springfield, and Delta moved the EUG departure 35 minutes earlier to 12:40. I have Hampton Eugene West/airport side Wednesday and a cancellable Springfield Gateway backup. Which one should I keep?

I need two details before I call it: what time does the Springfield breakfast end, and are you checking a bag? That decides whether the east-side hotel saves enough to offset the earlier airport buffer.
Breakfast is 7:30-8:45 at Springfield High. No checked bag. Boarding now says 12:05. I can leave the breakfast right at 8:50. Avis return at EUG.

Keep Hampton Eugene West. Switching to Springfield saves a little morning drive, but you already need to end near EUG, and the earlier flight makes the airport-side setup cleaner. Plan: check out before breakfast, leave the hotel 6:50, arrive Springfield about 7:20, depart 8:50, fuel on the way back, and aim for Avis return by 10:35. That gives roughly two hours before departure.
So do not go back to the hotel after breakfast? The Hampton breakfast starts at 6:30, but I will not have much time.

Do not go back. Pack Wednesday night, check out at 6:45, put luggage out of sight in the trunk, and treat hotel breakfast as coffee plus a grab-and-go item. If the counselor breakfast is light, use a quick Gateway coffee stop only if you are back on the road by 9:05.
Give me the final Thursday checklist, including fuel. And should I cancel Springfield now?

Yes, cancel Springfield Gateway now unless the breakfast host changes the location again. Thursday checklist: 6:45 check out Hampton Eugene West; 6:50 depart with luggage; 7:20 arrive Springfield; 8:50 leave even if conversation is still going; 9:15-9:30 fuel near Gateway or on Hwy 99 before EUG; 10:30-10:35 Avis return; 10:50 inside the terminal. Breakfast workaround: coffee or grab-and-go at Hampton, then rely on the event food. Keep fuel and parking receipts, and save the retimed Delta notice with the reimbursement file.
